## Why Estimates of the 1906 Earthquake Differ

One seismic analysis examined recordings from 96 observatories, then digitized and modeled usable data from 12. It suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.

A USGS team took a different approach, re-evaluating geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake. This method used ground deformation reflected in angles and distances between benchmarks, producing an estimate of 7.9.

The two estimates came from different methods of assessing the earthquake’s size, and those methods can disagree.
